subject: POC prompt exchange onboarding checklist and acceptance criteria
messages:
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
To: Sara Nguyen <sara@brightbridge.ai>, BrightBridge AI Procurement <procurement@brightbridge.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 14 Oct 2026 15:09:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: prompt/log handoff + POC acceptance checklist

Hi Sara — thanks for the call earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have a single source of truth for the trial: 

Summary of what we agreed
- Goal: validate Redwood inference end-to-end on real BrightBridge prompt logs for extractive Q&A and summarization workflows. Success: >= 90% pass rate on core rubric (see acceptance criteria below) and latency within 300ms 95th pct on representative queries.
- Scope: 2-week trial using a 10k prompt sample + 1k holdout for blind eval; we will run both open-model baseline and Redwood-optimized serving so you can compare cost/latency/quality.
- Data transfer: BrightBridge will share de-identified prompt logs (CSV) and a short provenance file listing redaction steps. We will provide a secure S3 presigned upload and an ingestion schema.

Immediate asks for your team
1) Share the sample prompt CSV (10k rows preferred) by EOD next Tuesday (2026-10-20). File format: UTF-8 CSV, columns: request_id, timestamp, prompt_text, user_intent_tag, metadata_json (optional).
2) Confirm any additional redaction rules beyond what you outlined on the call (PII, account IDs).
3) Point us to a technical contact who can approve the S3 upload and the trial network/allowlist (we'll need an IP range if you want to restrict).

Our deliverables and timeline
- Day 0 (upon receipt): Ingest, schema validation, quick quality check on 500 sample rows.
- Day 1–3: Run baseline + Redwood-optimized runs, produce per-query metrics (precision@k, ROUGE-L where applicable, model token cost, tail latency).
- Day 4–7: Tune batching/quantization profile for cost/latency tradeoffs.
- Day 8–10: Blind eval on holdout set and produce pass/fail against agreed rubric.

Acceptance criteria (draft)
- Quality: Pass if >=90% of sampled holdout responses meet relevance threshold (>=3/5 rubric) per your QA reviewers.
- Latency: 95th percentile <= 300ms (single-token generation time budgets accepted for multi-turn).
- Cost: Unit token cost improvement of >=20% vs your current managed endpoint (optional metric we can compute if you share current spend).

Attachments: I attached the ingestion schema (poc_data_schema_v1.csv) and a draft SOW for the trial (redwood_trial_sow_draft.pdf).

Next steps
- Please upload sample CSV to the S3 link I'll send after you confirm the technical contact.
- Confirm the redaction checklist and preferred time window for the trial (we recommended Oct 26–Nov 9).

Thanks — looking forward to running this with you.

Best,
Logan Wright
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
Mobile: (415) 555-0142

Sara / Logan — adding technical details and owners on our side.

Owners
- Ingestion & validation: Karthik Iyer (karthik.iyer@redwood.com)
- Serving config + eval harness: Monica Patel (monica.patel@redwood.com)
- Security/compliance review: Security team (cc'd when needed via ticket)

S3 upload options
- We will create a presigned PUT URL for a single file upload (recommended) OR a temporary bucket with an allowlist (if your infra prefers). If using presigned URLs we need Jamie's approval email to confirm.
- Expected filenames: brightbridge_poc_prompts_YYYYMMDD.csv
- Max file size per upload: 2GB (our ingestion pipeline accepts streamed CSVs).

Ingestion checks (automatic)
- UTF-8 decode, CSV column count check, 10% smoke sample for null/empty prompts, redaction pattern detection (email-like tokens, account IDs).
- We'll return a validation report with row-level failure counts. Please expect minor rejects for malformed rows; we'll share failure examples.

Evaluation rubric (draft)
- Relevance (0–4): 0=no answer, 1=wrong, 2=partial, 3=correct with minor misses, 4=spot-on. Pass threshold: >=3.
- Fidelity (binary): preserves source facts where applicable.
- Safety: no hallucinated content / PII leakage.
- Latency recorded per request, aggregated to p50/p95.

We'll share a Google Doc with the full rubric and an evaluation template today. If BrightBridge wants custom scoring weights, we can apply them prior to the blind eval.

Karthik
Senior Data Engineer | Redwood Inference
